clue.text: See 12
He will do time for money, so at moonlight, move soap

definitions.note: he who will swindle (do) someone; a noun for a con man

indicators.note: time for money tells us each letter standing for time is swapped out for the letter standing for money

parts.note: a moonlight flit is a secret move by night to dodge rent, so the move is a FLIT
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 money supply

indicators.note: so means likewise here: the same swap of time for money is made in the second word too, both times

parts.note: to soft-soap someone is to flatter them

explanation.surface: A crook's plan: serve time for the cash, then do a midnight flit while the soap opera is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do time' looks like prison, but 'do' belongs to the definition (swindle); 'time for money' swaps T for M in FLIT, and 'so' repeats the swap for both Ts of FLATTER. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is someone who will con, or do, people out of their money with trickery and nonsense.

clue.text: Perhaps 26 28 — can it now put off storms?

parts.note: 26 across is THE SUN, a British tabloid newspaper, and a tabloid is disparagingly called a rag

indicators.note: put off says these letters are removed from the word that clue 28 gives

parts.note: 28 across gives SHINES
can it! means be quiet, which is also said as sh
in means fashionable, current, of the now

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sunny spell might stop the bad weather from arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 26 and 28 together as 'the sun shines'; then 'Perhaps 26' gives RAG and 'can it now' (SH + IN) is taken from SHINES, leaving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to shout and rant angrily, which is exactly what someone who rages does.

clue.text: That's 1 Across here, oddly

indicators.note: 1 Across is the word FIRST, so this asks for the first letter of That's
oddly signals that the letters of here are arranged in an odd, unusual order

explanation.surface: A setter pointing out a quirk of numbering in this very grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is the third word of the linked answer FASTEST FINGER FIRST, so in this puzzle 'first' is number three, and three is itself odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The light at 1 Across completes a three-word phrase as its third part, so here it counts as number three.

clue.text: In expedition hands down tools to do one bolt

definitions.note: a single bolt from the sky in a storm

parts.note: expedition means great speed, and something done with lightning speed is done in expedition
workers who down tools go on strike

explanation.surface: Members of an expedition put down their kit so one of them can run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' suggests running away, but it is a thunderbolt; 'to do' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderbolt hitting the ground is a single flash of electrical discharge from a storm cloud.

clue.text: Waste no time cutting the odds!

definitions.meaning: a call to hurry because each moment matters
if you cut out the odd-numbered items, only each even-numbered one is kept and matters

explanation.surface: Urging speed when the chances are against you, like a gambler against a ticking clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: drop the odd ones and only the alternate, even-placed items still count.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom urging haste, and read literally it says only alternate items are tallied.

clue.text: Work ache, say? I take this seat?

definitions.note: a comfortable armchair, the kind you sink into

indicators.note: work here is an imperative to rework the letters into new shape

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone with a backache from work wondering whether to sit down here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun causing the ache, but it signals the anagram of ACHE SAY I plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, upholstered armchair is just the seat for someone with an aching back to relax in.

clue.text: Select old ones like this Nimrod's not once initially enjoyed

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: not once says one occurrence of the letter is struck out

parts.note: this is a clue, so ones like it are clues
the setter Nimrod speaking would say I have, contracted to I've

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word enjoyed

explanation.surface: The setter boasting that a select band of old-style clues were once never enjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something select is restricted to a privileged few, open only to chosen members.

clue.text: Not a year for upsetting that local

definitions.note: a dialect or poetic word for that, used in regional speech

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the letters upside down, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: not a, as in not a single one, means no

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a year without a single upset is unusual for the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub but signals dialect; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is a regional or archaic word meaning that or those, still heard in northern English and Scots speech.

clue.text: Pretentious — did you hear? — twinning this Israeli port with Luton?

indicators.note: twinning with Luton suggests the pair of names together make the sound, so separating them leaves the port
did you hear asks us to go by how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: highfalutin means pompous or pretentious

explanation.surface: A sarcastic question about whether a grand foreign port would ever be twinned with an unglamorous English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, the Israeli port plus Luton (a town north of London) sounds like 'highfalutin'; take away the Luton part to leave the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a major Mediterranean seaport city in northern Israel.

clue.text: See 12
See 5
See 27
Express digital ordering exercise of questionable character?

definitions.text: Express digital ordering exercise of questionable character?

parts.words: Express digital ordering exercise of questionable character?
parts.note: the round on the TV quiz Who Wants to Be a Millionaire where contestants race with their ... to put items in order; it is a question round

explanation.walkthrough: On Who Wants to Be a Millionaire, contestants competed to be quickest at keying answers into the right order to win the hot seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiz round is a speed test of digits pressing buttons in sequence, set by quizmasters' questions.

clue.text: See 27
See 5
Court action to hear witness — a new Statesman

indicators.note: to hear asks for the spelling of what these words sound like when spoken

parts.note: tennis is the game played on a court
to witness is to see

explanation.surface: A trial in which a court hears a witness, then a new politician steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'Statesman' suggest law and politics; the court is a tennis court and a Statesman is someone from one of the US states.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tennessee is a person from that American state, so a Statesman in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: Being besotted with dad's ex, hit it off and ran abroad to conquer America

indicators.note: to conquer, the jumbled letters take over by surrounding the letter for America
abroad means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A young man obsessed with his father's former partner, who got on with him then fled to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' scrambles the fodder into FTHERFIXTION, and 'to conquer' wraps that round A for America; 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An unhealthy obsession with one's father is a psychological attachment, a kind of infatuation centred on a parent.

clue.text: Sheriff's 10 shot so darned uncompromising!

indicators.note: 10 across is SECOND, so this asks for the second letter of the word Sheriff
shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A sheriff's deputy shooting and cursing in a tough Western standoff.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the answer at 10 across, SECOND, so Sheriff's second letter, H, starts the word; the rest rearranges SO DARNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tough and unsentimental, who won't bend to emotion or pressure, is called hard-nosed.

clue.text: With dad in tears, former partner makes business even bigger

definitions.note: enlarges a company again; a verb phrase matching the verb form

indicators.note: in tells us the partner and father are placed inside the word for tears

parts.note: tears means rips, rends
an ex is a former partner
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A tearful family scene in which an ex makes a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like crying, but it is the verb that rips; 'With' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow a company again, after an earlier growth, is to enlarge it a second time.

clue.text: I make an impression, busy trade and green produce

definitions.note: the clue is spoken by the grower, so I is the person described

parts.note: to mark something is to make an impression on it

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters bustling about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A self-portrait of a grower who leaves a mark and does a busy trade selling vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the grower talking, so 'I' is the definition and the rest a description; 'busy' rearranges TRADE GREEN, with 'produce' supporting the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The speaker grows vegetables and fruit commercially to sell at markets, so the speaker is that grower.

clue.text: Scotland's last flower

definitions.meaning: the last letter of Scotland is D

explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a crossword's usual trick for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter name and a Scottish river both use this spelling, so the word answers both readings.

clue.text: Pact partners initially will pen concerning new union

indicators.note: pen means enclose, as in a sheep pen, so the outer letters surround the rest

parts.note: two partners, so two initial letters, P and P
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Two people about to marry agree to sign a contract about their new union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing, but it signals enclosing; both partners give their initial P.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenuptial agreement is a contract a couple sign before marriage settling assets in case of divorce.

clue.text: Once got issue rejected

indicators.note: rejected, thrown back, signals that the letters are read backwards

parts.note: got as in understood, saw
to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: A complaint that a problem was once dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in former times, formerly, as an old-fashioned way of saying long ago.

clue.text: Foremost of maestri so up and down with movement

indicators.note: foremost of picks the leading letter of maestri
in a down clue, so read going up then going down gives the same pair both ways

parts.note: the word so read upward then downward, which forms a palindrome

explanation.surface: A conductor guiding an orchestra through a piece, waving the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue SO going up reads OS and going down reads SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosso is an Italian musical direction meaning animated, lively, played with motion.

clue.text: We listen in hush, she is raving: an opportune time to …

indicators.note: raving means wild and mad, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic woman ranting while everyone else keeps quiet and listens.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'make hay while the sun shines'; the ellipsis leads into 27, where the sleepy version continues. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb urges seizing the moment, so the phrase names the favourable chance to act.

clue.text: Scottish port's dry, Sassenachs might say?

indicators.note: Sassenach is a Scots word for the English; this asks how English speakers pronounce it

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it

explanation.surface: A sneer that a Scottish harbour town is dull, the kind of remark the English might make.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland; ''s' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a harbour town on the Firth of Clyde in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: See 24
… retire?!

parts.note: continuing 24: after making ... while it is sunny, a cheeky twist on the ... leads to going to bed

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 24: instead of 'make hay while the sun shines', the hay here is for sleeping on.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for going to bed, from the days when mattresses were stuffed with dried grass.

clue.text: See 24
Blue backs mobbing our home scorer

indicators.note: mobbing means crowding around, so the reversed word surrounds the other
backs here means goes backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: blue means sad
for a British setter, home is the UK

explanation.surface: Sad football defenders crowding round the home team's goal scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' looks like sport; it is a composer, Paul Dukas of The Sorcerer's Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes musical scores, and Paul Dukas was a French composer.

clue.text: Very good point about bustles

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: so, said in answer, means very good, I agree, as in 'so be it'
a point is a dot

explanation.surface: Praise for a sharp point in an argument about busy activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusses and commotions are both a busy stir of activity, the sense of hustle and fuss.

clue.text: The drink last in line nobody is able to swallow

parts.note: nobody is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: to swallow means take inside, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: last in points to the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: A drinking contest: the last one in the queue can't down their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, not a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea is informally called the drink, as in falling into the drink.
